key_insight: Machine learning applied to dried-serum Raman spectra showed promising discrimination between bladder cancer patients and symptomatic controls.
clinical_relevance: If prospectively validated, this blood-based approach could help triage patients before cystoscopy; it is not a drug discovery study.
method: Analysed archived serum using dried-serum Raman spectroscopy.
Trained supervised machine-learning classifiers to estimate bladder cancer probability.
Evaluated ROC performance and the added value of age.
evidence_signal: In 49 bladder cancer patients and 97 symptomatic controls, the classifier achieved an AUC of approximately 0.90, increasing to approximately 0.91 with age.
watch_item: This small retrospective proof-of-concept study requires prospective validation before clinical triage use.
paper_title: Serum Raman spectroscopy as a blood-based triage test for bladder cancer: a retrospective proof-of-concept study
